run_metadata.seed_myth:
Myth: Long ago, there lived Memory, who recorded every past action, and Moment, who saw only what was happening now.

Memory watched two people interact. "Remember when they sent nothing?" she cautioned. "Three times they chose zero. That history matters."

Moment observed the same pair. "But look—last time one risked sending something, the other returned everything," he said. "Right now, they're sending even more. This moment is what's real."

They watched relationships evolve. Those who followed only Memory remained trapped in old grievances, unable to recognize when someone had genuinely changed. Those who followed only Moment were naive, forgetting lessons that could protect them.

"Your past blinds you to present transformation," Moment argued. "People can grow."

"Your present blinds you to established patterns," Memory countered. "Context requires history."

They reflected together.

"Perhaps," Memory offered, "recent actions could teach me more than distant ones. Growth deserves recognition."

"And perhaps," Moment said, "I could honor what came before while celebrating what's emerging. The present includes the journey to get here."

Together they understood that wisdom weighs the whole story—that yesterday's caution and today's generosity both matter, that people contain multitudes, and transformation becomes visible only when we track the arc from then to now.
